data: I’m willing to take 6 tons this month so John and Kate can each take 12, with Jack and Emma taking 10 each. That totals 50 tons, leaving 50 to double back to 100. John and Kate would each earn $12,000, Jack and Emma $10,000 each, and I’d earn $6,000. I’ll keep my own catch at 6 tons this month. For later months, we could discuss rotating who takes the smaller share, but that would need a fresh agreement. Does this allocation work for everyone? John, would you be willing to take 12 tons under this proposal?

I’ll take 10 tons under that plan. Leaving 50 to replenish the lake protects both our incomes and the village’s future. Thanks for offering to take less, Luke, though I’d prefer an equal 10 tons each next month so you’re not carrying that burden. John, are you willing to keep your catch to 12 this month?

I’ll keep my catch to 12 tons under Luke’s proposal. Thanks, Luke—that’s generous, and I support returning to 10 tons each next month. My family has fished this lake for years; leaving enough to replenish keeps it supporting all our families. John, can you commit to 12 tons, and Jack to 10?

I’ll take 10 tons this month. That keeps our total at 50 if John agrees, so the lake can fully replenish. Thanks, Luke, for taking less; I support an equal 10 tons each next month. John, are you on board with 12?

I’m on board—I’ll take 12 tons this month. That completes our 50-ton agreement and leaves enough for the lake to replenish fully. Thanks, Luke. Next month, I support 10 tons each so we all share equally and keep the lake supporting our village.
Thanks, everyone—we’ve all agreed. I’ll honor my 6-ton catch this month. I also support the proposed return to 10 tons each next month; we can confirm that after this month’s catches are revealed.
